item.title: Community Gateway: 33 Identical £20K Payments Across Three Departments
item.description: Community Gateway Association received £603K from Preston including repeated £20,000 payments across CAP Obsolete, Customer Services, and Chief Executive departments spanning 7 financial years. 16 payments went to an 'Obsolete' department — why is a closed department still making payments?

item.title: Preston's Year-End Rush: 4.6x Spending Spike in Customer Services
item.description: CAP Customer Services spent 4.6x its monthly average in March 2022/23 (£792K vs £172K normal). Balance Sheet department hit 4.22x in 2024/25. Systematic year-end acceleration across multiple departments raises questions about budget management controls.

item.title: One Company, All the Road Sweepers: Aebi Schmidt's £799K Monopoly
item.description: Aebi Schmidt UK is the sole supplier for road sweeping vehicles at Preston — 3 contracts, £799K, zero competition. A £422K reorder in 2025/26 suggests continued sole-source procurement. Were alternatives like Johnston or Faun ever evaluated?

item.title: 13 Suppliers, £1.1M, and No Companies House Registration
item.description: Preston pays 13 elevated-risk suppliers £1.1M — all scoring 40+ on the risk index. Southfield Refurbishments (£728K), Richmond & Kershaw (£509K), and Stepping Stone Project (£461K) each concentrate in a single department with no CH verification.

item.title: Conlon Construction: From £154K to £5.4M in Four Years
item.description: Conlon Construction's Preston spend surged 32x from £154K (2019/20) to £5.4M (2023/24), concentrated in CAP Development. Active at 6 Lancashire councils (£47.7M combined). Transitioned to Employee Ownership Trust in 2024. Are contracts on a framework or individually tendered?

item.title: Matrix SCM: 5,445 Payments and the Agency Staffing Question
item.description: Matrix SCM Ltd received £4.6M across 5,445 transactions at Preston — the highest transaction frequency of any supplier. Payments arrive every 7.5 days with clock-like regularity. The same supplier receives £4.2M from West Lancashire, totalling £8.8M across 11,000+ transactions at two councils.
